raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

In deterministic mode on ROCm every custom all-reduce runs the 1-stage kernel: each GPU reads every peer's whole input and sums the ranks in the order 0..n-1. That order is what makes the result independent of the input size, but each GPU reads n times the data, so at TP4/TP8 the all-reduce takes a large share of the step: on MI350X, Qwen3-8B deterministic decode/prefill spends 48% of GPU time in it at TP4 and 63% at TP8 (8k-token inputs), and deterministic throughput at TP8 was about half of normal mode. The 2-stage kernel (reduce-scatter + all-gather) reads far less, but it cannot be used as is: each owner starts its sum at its own rank, so an element's result depends on which rank owns it, which changes with the input size. This PR adds a fixed-order option to the 2-stage kernel that sums the ranks in the same order as the 1-stage kernel, so the two give the same bits for every element at every size, and uses it for large inputs at 4 and 8 ranks. Results do not change; on MI350X deterministic throughput rises 16-24% at TP4 and 29-57% at TP8 on Qwen3-8B, and 28-54% at TP8 on Qwen3.8-27B, with every determinism check passing.

## Modifications

- `custom_all_reduce_hip.cuh`: `cross_device_reduce_2stage` gets a template parameter `kFixedOrder` (default `false`, so normal mode is unchanged). With it, stage 1 reads the ranks in the order 0..n-1 instead of starting at its own rank; stage 2 (the gather) is unchanged.
- `deterministic_all_reduce.hip`: one templated launcher instead of three copies per dtype. Inputs copied into the registered buffer (`deterministic_all_reduce_unreg`, which every deterministic call of `CustomAllreduce` uses for inputs that fit the buffer, including in CUDA graphs and the pieces of larger inputs) take the fixed-order 2-stage kernel with 32 blocks at or above 512 KiB at 4 ranks and 256 KiB at 8 ranks (the thresholds `CustomAllreduce::allreduce` uses); everything else keeps the 1-stage kernel with 16 blocks: smaller inputs, 2 and 6 ranks, and `deterministic_all_reduce_reg` (its inputs can be larger than the IPC buffer that the 2-stage kernel stages 1/n of the input in).
- New test `test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_amd_deterministic_allreduce_fixed_order.py` (`stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x`): at 4 and 8 ranks, bf16 and fp16, sizes on both sides of the thresholds, eager and CUDA graphs, the all-reduce output must equal, bit for bit, the sum of the ranks' inputs computed in torch in the order 0..n-1 (float32 accumulation). The data is chosen so its float32 sum depends on the order of the ranks.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, ROCm 7.2.4, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261021`.

Kernel level (bf16, hidden 4096 and 7168, 1-2,040 rows eager and 1-512 rows in CUDA graphs, order-sensitive data, 2/4/8 ranks): the fixed-order 2-stage kernel's output equals the current 1-stage kernel's output bit for bit at every size, is identical on every rank, and a row's result does not depend on the number of rows. Control: the current (unordered) 2-stage kernel differs from the 1-stage kernel at 42-44 of 42-44 sizes at 4 and 8 ranks.

End to end, deterministic mode (`--enable-deterministic-inference`, Triton prefill and AITER decode attention, together with the other open MI350X deterministic-mode PRs), `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic` (`single`, `prefix`, `prefix --return-logprob`, `radix_cache`, 50 trials) plus a bitwise batch-size check (the same prompt in batches of 1 to 50, 1,275 responses, token IDs and logprobs compared exactly with the batch-size-1 response): every check passes (`single` 1 output, `prefix` 1/1/1/1, prefix logprobs identical, radix cache consistent, bitwise 1,275 / 1,275). With this branch's build (sgl-kernel rebuilt for gfx950):

- the new test passes at 4 and 8 ranks, and the existing 2-rank deterministic all-reduce test passes;
- every check above passes on Qwen3-8B TP2, TP4 and TP8, Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4, Qwen3.8-27B TP4 and Qwen3.8-27B TP8, and again on fresh servers: Qwen3-8B TP8 4 / 4, Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 3 / 3, Qwen3.8-27B TP4 2 / 2;
- GSM8K (sgl-eval 0.1.2, temperature 0, 1,319 questions) is unchanged: Qwen3-8B 93.40% / 93.25% / 93.48% at TP2 / TP4 / TP8 (93.48% at TP8 before), Qwen3.8-27B 96.21% at TP4 and 96.13% at TP8.

Through the experiment-only switch (same kernel and selection) the checks also passed on Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 with GSM8K 95.15% (95.15% before).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel time per all-reduce (bf16, hidden 4096, CUDA graph of 50 calls, median of 7), current 1-stage kernel vs this PR:

| input | 8 ranks: current | 8 ranks: this PR | 4 ranks: current | 4 ranks: this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 MiB (128 rows) | 23.9 us | 15.4 us (1.55x) | 22.2 us | 16.2 us (1.37x) |
| 4 MiB (512 rows) | 77.8 us | 31.4 us (2.47x) | 74.8 us | 43.1 us (1.74x) |
| 8 MiB (1,024 rows) | 149.2 us | 50.7 us (2.94x) | 144.5 us | 77.8 us (1.86x) |
| 16 MiB (2,040 rows) | 291.5 us | 88.1 us (3.31x) | 283.1 us | 146.0 us (1.94x) |

Below the thresholds (decode-size inputs) the 1-stage kernel is faster and is kept; at 2 ranks the two kernels are equally fast and the 1-stage kernel is kept.

End to end, deterministic mode, `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, output throughput, current vs this branch's build (same server arguments, interleaved):

| model, TP | 1k in / 1k out | 8k in / 1k out | 32k in / 256 out | long context |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B, 2 | 10,135 -> 10,145 (+0.1%) | 2,623 -> 2,624 (0.0%) | 207.2 -> 207.3 (0.0%) | |
| Qwen3-8B, 4 | 15,543 -> 18,129 (+16.6%) | 3,946 -> 4,755 (+20.5%) | 303.4 -> 377.5 (+24.4%) | 64k / 120k: 125.2 -> 149.3 (+19.2%) / 30.8 -> 36.2 (+17.5%) |
| Qwen3-8B, 8 | 20,147 -> 26,751 (+32.8%) | 5,044 -> 7,409 (+46.9%) | 383.3 -> 600.6 (+56.7%) | 64k / 120k: 160.1 -> 233.9 (+46.1%) / 41.7 -> 60.0 (+43.9%) |
| Qwen3.8-27B, 8 | 7,635 -> 9,803 (+28.4%) | 2,191 -> 3,196 (+45.9%) | 165.2 -> 254.9 (+54.3%) | |

(tok/s; 256 / 256 / 64 prompts; long context 64k in / 256 out and 120k in / 128 out, Qwen3-8B with YaRN.) Qwen3-8B TP8 is the mean of two rounds: the current kernel gave the same throughput in both (20,136 / 20,158 at 1k in / 1k out), this PR 27,503 and 25,999 (+36.6% and +29.0%); at 8k and 32k the two rounds agree within 0.3%. TP2 is unchanged because the 1-stage kernel is kept at 2 ranks. Time to first token falls 19-47% at TP4 and TP8 (Qwen3.8-27B TP8: 5.6 -> 3.3 s, 22.9 -> 13.3 s, 13.5 -> 8.2 s). Normal mode is unchanged.

Through the experiment-only switch running the same kernel and selection, before the build: Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 15,024 -> 16,431 (+9.4%) / 4,435 -> 5,089 (+14.7%) / 334.6 -> 393.1 (+17.5%); Qwen3.8-27B TP4 5,517 -> 6,245 (+13.2%) / 1,776 -> 2,160 (+21.6%) / 131.8 -> 164.2 (+24.6%), 64k / 128k +21.8% / +22.8%.

Related: #34543 (merged) reduces deterministic inputs larger than the buffer piece by piece through `deterministic_all_reduce_unreg`, so those pieces also take the faster kernel. The measurements above include it in both columns, and this branch merges cleanly on current main.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@HaiShaw CI passes and approved by @hubertlu-tw. Could you merge please.

I reproduced the kernel-level numbers on 8x MI355X (gfx950) with [benchmark_rocm.py](https://github.com/hubertlu-tw/sglang/blob/cc36b182efae2b1e4b90eb6d542da669ab99b53e/benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_rocm.py), building sgl-kernel from the base (8252e3af63) and from this PR, and running the deterministic path (`SGLANG_USE_1STAGE_ALLREDUCE=1`, bf16, 16 MiB buffer).

Above the thresholds the fixed-order 2-stage kernel is clearly faster. In CUDA graph mode TP4 goes from 1.19x at 512 KiB to 1.88x at 16 MiB (317 to 169 us), and TP8 goes from 1.30x at 512 KiB to 3.03x at 16 MiB (326 to 107 us). Eager mode shows the same trend (1.84x and 2.97x at 16 MiB). TP2 and all sizes below the thresholds are unchanged, and normal mode stays within run-to-run noise. In one run TP8 at exactly 256 KiB looked slightly slower, but three interleaved repeats came out break-even (0.98-1.01x), so the threshold sits right at the crossover rather than past it. The PR's bitwise test passes at TP4/TP8, and a manual fp32 check matches RCCL exactly.

A few small follow-ups that don't need to block this PR: the new test also passes against the base kernel, which has no 2-stage path, so it can't catch the 2-stage kernel never being selected. Checking for cross_device_reduce_2stage in a profiler trace, or adding the unordered 2-stage kernel as a negative control, would close that gap. `DET_AR_CASE(6)` instantiates a 2-stage kernel that never runs, since 6 ranks always take 1-stage, so case 6 can launch 1-stage directly like case 2. And the comment on `deterministic_all_reduce_reg `should say its input isn't bounded by `max_size`, so nobody later turns on the 2-stage path there without a size check. A quick spot check on MI300X would also be good, since the 32-block setting was tuned on MI350X. I'd expect it to work correctly there, but the speedup may be smaller.

detail.title: [Perf] [AMD] deterministic: Use a fixed-order two-stage all-reduce for large inputs

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,132 @@
+"""The deterministic custom all-reduce on ROCm must sum every element over the ranks in
+the order 0..world_size-1, whatever the input size: it switches from the 1-stage to the
+2-stage kernel above a size threshold, and both must give exactly that sum. Checked bit
+for bit against the same sum computed with torch, at 4 and 8 ranks, in eager mode and in
+CUDA graphs, with data whose float32 sum depends on the order of the ranks.
+"""
+
+import multiprocessing as mp
+import os
+import socket
+import sys
+import traceback
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_hip
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=120, suite="stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x")
+
+HIDDEN = 4096
+# Rows of HIDDEN bf16 values; 32 rows (256 KiB) and 64 rows (512 KiB) are the 2-stage
+# thresholds at 8 and 4 ranks. The largest size stays under the 16 MiB buffer.
+EAGER_ROWS = (1, 7, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 128, 500, 1024, 2047)
+GRAPH_ROWS = (1, 16, 32, 64, 256)
+
+
+def _open_port():
+    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
+        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        return s.getsockname()[1]
+
+
+def _order_sensitive(rows, dtype, rank):
+    # Values of magnitude 2^12, 1 and 2^-12 with random signs: their float32 sum over the
+    # ranks rounds differently in a different order (randn data would hide that).
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(1000 * rank + rows)
+    exp = torch.tensor([12.0, 0.0, -12.0])[
+        torch.randint(0, 3, (rows, HIDDEN), generator=g)
+    ]
+    sign = torch.randint(0, 2, (rows, HIDDEN), generator=g) * 2 - 1
+    return (sign * exp.exp2() * (1 + torch.rand(rows, HIDDEN, generator=g))).to(dtype)
+
+
+def _fixed_order_sum(x, world_size):
+    parts = [torch.empty_like(x) for _ in range(world_size)]
+    dist.all_gather(parts, x)
+    acc = parts[0].float()
+    for p in parts[1:]:
+        acc = acc + p.float()
+    return acc.to(x.dtype)
+
+
+def _worker(world_size, rank, port, failures):
+    try:
+        os.environ["SGLANG_USE_1STAGE_ALLREDUCE"] = (
+            "1"  # selects the deterministic path
+        )
+        torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
+        dist.init_process_group(
+            "nccl",
+            init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}",
+            rank=rank,
+            world_size=world_size,
+        )
+        from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce import (
+            CustomAllreduce,
+        )
+
+        car = CustomAllreduce(
+            dist.new_group(backend="gloo"), torch.device("cuda", rank)
+        )
+        assert not car.disabled and car.use_amd_deterministic_impl
+        for dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16):
+            for rows in EAGER_ROWS:
+                x = _order_sensitive(rows, dtype, rank).cuda()
+                out = car.custom_all_reduce(x)
+                ref = _fixed_order_sum(x, world_size)
+                if not torch.equal(out, ref):
+                    failures.put(
+                        f"{world_size} ranks, rank {rank}, {dtype}, eager, {rows} rows"
+                    )
+            with car.capture():
+                graphs = {}
+                for rows in GRAPH_ROWS:
+                    static_in = torch.zeros(rows, HIDDEN, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+                    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+                    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+                        static_out = car.custom_all_reduce(static_in)
+                    graphs[rows] = (graph, static_in, static_out)
+            for rows, (graph, static_in, static_out) in graphs.items():
+                x = _order_sensitive(rows, dtype, rank).cuda()
+                static_in.copy_(x)
+                graph.replay()
+                torch.cuda.synchronize()
+                if not torch.equal(static_out, _fixed_order_sum(x, world_size)):
+                    failures.put(
+                        f"{world_size} ranks, rank {rank}, {dtype}, graph, {rows} rows"
+                    )
+        car.close()
+        dist.destroy_process_group()
+    except Exception:
+        failures.put(f"rank {rank}: {traceback.format_exc()}")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_hip(), reason="ROCm deterministic all-reduce")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("world_size", [4, 8])
+def test_fixed_rank_order_at_every_size(world_size):
+    if torch.cuda.device_count() < world_size:
+        pytest.skip(f"needs {world_size} GPUs")
+    ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
+    failures = ctx.Queue()
+    port = _open_port()
+    procs = [
+        ctx.Process(target=_worker, args=(world_size, rank, port, failures))
+        for rank in range(world_size)
+    ]
+    for p in procs:
+        p.start()
+    for p in procs:
+        p.join(timeout=600)
+    found = []
+    while not failures.empty():
+        found.append(failures.get())
+    assert all(p.exitcode == 0 for p in procs), found
+    assert not found, "\n".join(found)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

reviews.body:
I reproduced the kernel-level numbers on 8x MI355X (gfx950) with [benchmark_rocm.py](https://github.com/hubertlu-tw/sglang/blob/cc36b182efae2b1e4b90eb6d542da669ab99b53e/benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_rocm.py), building sgl-kernel from the base (8252e3af63) and from this PR, and running the deterministic path (`SGLANG_USE_1STAGE_ALLREDUCE=1`, bf16, 16 MiB buffer).

Above the thresholds the fixed-order 2-stage kernel is clearly faster. In CUDA graph mode TP4 goes from 1.19x at 512 KiB to 1.88x at 16 MiB (317 to 169 us), and TP8 goes from 1.30x at 512 KiB to 3.03x at 16 MiB (326 to 107 us). Eager mode shows the same trend (1.84x and 2.97x at 16 MiB). TP2 and all sizes below the thresholds are unchanged, and normal mode stays within run-to-run noise. In one run TP8 at exactly 256 KiB looked slightly slower, but three interleaved repeats came out break-even (0.98-1.01x), so the threshold sits right at the crossover rather than past it. The PR's bitwise test passes at TP4/TP8, and a manual fp32 check matches RCCL exactly.

A few small follow-ups that don't need to block this PR: the new test also passes against the base kernel, which has no 2-stage path, so it can't catch the 2-stage kernel never being selected. Checking for cross_device_reduce_2stage in a profiler trace, or adding the unordered 2-stage kernel as a negative control, would close that gap. `DET_AR_CASE(6)` instantiates a 2-stage kernel that never runs, since 6 ranks always take 1-stage, so case 6 can launch 1-stage directly like case 2. And the comment on `deterministic_all_reduce_reg `should say its input isn't bounded by `max_size`, so nobody later turns on the 2-stage path there without a size check. A quick spot check on MI300X would also be good, since the 32-block setting was tuned on MI350X. I'd expect it to work correctly there, but the speedup may be smaller.
